Subject: Questions on Exhibit B tiering and surcharge smoothing

Aisha —

Thanks for sending the contract bundle. Our procurement team ran the pricing schedule past finance and we have two areas that need clarification before we can move to legal sign-off:

1) Rounding and per-unit math: Exhibit B shows per-1k-token unit pricing in tiers, but the order form references "per-request" billing in the billing schema. That creates ambiguity for multi-turn chat sessions where token counts don't split neatly into 1k units. Would Redwood confirm whether invoices will round per-request (to nearest cent) or aggregate usage monthly and then round? Example: 3,450 tokens at $0.0025/1k — do you charge on 3.45 units or round per-request?

2) Surcharge smoothing / cap: Our legal noticed the surcharge clause (Section 4.2) that allows temporary surcharges during capacity spikes. We need a clear floor/cap for surcharges and an amortization mechanism across invoice periods so we don't get a surprise one-off 40% surcharge on a single monthly bill.

Attached: our annotated billing worksheet (Pricing_Schedule_Worksheet.xlsx) with examples. Can your team propose language amendments that make invoicing predictable and map back to Exhibit B line items?

We'd like to close this this week if possible.

Thanks,
Sam Jennings
Director, Procurement — Novus Health

Subject: Re: Questions on Exhibit B tiering and surcharge smoothing

Sam —

Appreciate the clear examples and the worksheet — very helpful. High-level response below; copies of Legal and Pricing are on this thread to propose clean redline language.

- Rounding: Redwood invoices aggregate customer usage per billing period (calendar month) and apply unit pricing to the aggregated quantity. We do not round per individual request by default. That said, the Order Form should be explicit: we can add a clause that states "Usage is aggregated per calendar month, converted to pricing units as specified in Exhibit B, and rounded to the nearest cent on the invoice." That addresses the multi-turn ambiguity.

- Surcharge smoothing/cap: We agree a one-off surprise is undesirable. Two quick options from Pricing:
  1) Hard cap on surcharge as a percent of the monthly invoice (e.g., max 15% additional to monthly invoice) plus a quarterly true-up; or
  2) Allow up to 35% temporary surcharge but amortize the overage across the next three invoices (spread evenly) with a maximum per-invoice uplift of 12%.

Marissa — can you suggest redline language for Exhibit B (rounding, and a surcharge smoothing paragraph with example math)? Ben — FYI on the two options; we need your commercial view on acceptability. Sam — happy to schedule quick call if that helps.

Thanks,
Aisha Rahman

Folks —

Thanks — attached is a redline (OrderForm_ExhibitB_redline_v3.pdf) that implements the aggregation + rounding language and a surcharge-smoothing clause. Key points I inserted (high level):

1) Usage aggregation + rounding: "Customer usage shall be aggregated per calendar month and converted to the pricing unit set forth in Exhibit B. After applying the applicable tiered per-unit rate, the resulting invoice amount shall be rounded to the nearest cent. For avoidance of doubt, Redwood will not perform per-request rounding unless otherwise agreed in writing."

2) Tier-split interpretation: define "tier band" math so the per-unit price applies pro rata across the portion of usage that falls into each band (no step-function cliff charging). Added explicit example showing 3,450 tokens split across bands and resulting calculations.

3) Surcharge safeguard: propose the following operational language —
  - Temporary capacity surcharges are limited to a maximum of 30% of the monthly invoice in any single billing period.
  - If a temporary surcharge is applied, Redwood shall notify Customer within five business days and amortize any surcharge amount that exceeds 10% of that invoice over the next two consecutive invoices.
  - The Customer’s total monthly uplift from surcharge amortization shall not exceed 15% of the then-current invoice in any subsequent month.

Rationale: this gives Novus protection from single-month shocks while letting Redwood recover temporary excess costs. I included worked examples in the redline.

Sam — if the percentages are too high/low, we can iterate. Ben — per commercial guidance we may accept smaller cap first-year and revisit at renewal; I left a comment in the PDF to that effect.

Attachments: OrderForm_ExhibitB_redline_v3.pdf (redline), Pricing_Schedule_Worksheet.xlsx (reference)

Best,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Corporate Counsel — Redwood Inference

All —

Thanks Marissa, the redline looks great as a starting point. From a deal perspective Novus is price-sensitive; I want to propose a compromise that smooths Novus' onboarding risk while protecting Redwood:

- Pilot year concession: cap temporary surcharges to 20% for the first 12 months from contract effective date, with amortization across two invoices if the surcharge exceeds 8% for any invoice.
- At the 12-month anniversary we do a usage review and either: (a) lift to the standard 30% cap, or (b) formalize a custom surcharge cap based on observed utilization patterns.

If Novus accepts the pilot-year concession, we absorb a bit more short-term exposure which helps them to migrate. If they push for a permanent 20% cap we may need to add a minimum monthly commitment increase or an annual price uplift.

Sam — does that sound workable? If yes I can approve the redline with the pilot-year carve and we route the PDF for signature.

Cheers,
